The worker runs this script as the account it runs as, once per reference before the container starts. Only declare a resolver you trust.

What a run gets

A trigger's profile
run.secrets names at most 16 variables. Each reference is resolved before the container starts, through run.secretsProfile or default, once per reference.
A project's bundle
secretBundles in the triggers file binds a project to a bundle resolver. It prints dotenv or json once per job start: at most 64 variables, 256 KiB of output and 64 KiB per value. A trigger's explicit run.secrets win on a clash; the run record names the variables received and shadowed.
When a run goes without its bundle
A hand run, a chained run, an opted-out trigger (run.secretBundle: false), a pull request from a fork without forkReviews, or a pull request whose head could not be verified. The run's page says which.
The resolver behind both
An executable at an absolute path, declared in PI_SECRET_PROFILES or PI_SECRET_BUNDLES in the .env, or secretProfiles or secretBundles in the settings overlay. It runs on the host as the worker's account. An overlay resolver must be inside PI_SECRET_RESOLVER_ROOTS. A name declared in both sources refuses every secrets or bundled job. The resolver's own credential never enters the job.
Where the variables sit
On local and podman, the job can read every value. On OpenShell venues, a variable with an endpoint is a placeholder that the gateway swaps for its value only in a request to that host. A forge job also receives its forge token, each job its provider's credential when required, and whatever PI_FORWARD_ENV forwards. Connections names their sources.
Never shown here
A reference, a secret value, or a resolver's or root's full path. Resolver previews show only each path's last folder. Names and states only.
